summary: Pre-production verification of Spazio Sicuro after CORS/lifespan/rate-limit/honeypot/Resend/SEO/privacy-page changes. BACKEND: pytest suite expanded to 27 tests (25 in backend_test.py + 2 in new test_rate_limit.py), all passing when run serially (-n 0). Covered: GET /api/ + /api/health (200, healthy), lifespan startup log ('Spazio Sicuro API — startup' present in supervisor logs, no on_event deprecation), POST /api/contact valid payload -> 200 + id(uuid) + created_at ISO + MongoDB persistence verified via pymongo (all fields match, no _id leaked), minimal payload, honeypot ('website' filled) -> fake 200 with random uuid and ZERO documents in MongoDB (verified by message/email/id count == 0, plus log 'Honeypot triggered'), honeypot empty string treated as human and persisted with no 'website' field stored, 8 validation cases -> 422 (bad email, message <5 chars, message >4000, missing fields), downloads basic/full-app/pdf/pdf-full -> 200 with correct content-type/content-disposition and real magic bytes (PK / %PDF), 5 invalid keys (incl. path traversal '../server.py') -> 404, /tool.html no longer served as standalone page. Resend: RESEND_API_KEY empty -> log 'Email notification skipped (RESEND_API_KEY or OWNER_EMAIL missing)' with no exception, request unaffected. RATE LIMIT works (5/hour then 429) but is keyed on the WRONG IP behind the ingress (see critical issue). FRONTEND (desktop 1920x1080 + mobile 390x844): landing loads, no console errors, no horizontal overflow; title/description/lang='it' meta correct; nav shows exactly 7 links (Manifesto, Come funziona, Genitori, Scuole, Privacy, FAQ, Contatti) + 'Entra' CTA and NO Download link; nav 'Privacy' scrolls to landing #privacy section (path stays '/', hash '#privacy', privacy-title absent); footer-privacy (href=/privacy) navigates to /privacy page with h1 'Privacy Policy'; deep-link /privacy renders correctly; back-home returns to landing; contact form submit -> 'Grazie. Ti risponderemo appena possibile.' + form reset (desktop and mobile); honeypot input present but rendered at x=-9999 (off-screen, not reachable by users); help FAB dialog shows 4 emergency tel: links (112, 19696, 0223272327, 800861061) and closes via Escape, outside click and X; mobile hamburger drawer shows 7 links, scrolls to target and closes.

critical.issue: Rate limiting is keyed on request.client.host (slowapi get_remote_address), which behind the k8s/Cloudflare ingress is the PROXY POD IP (observed 10.66.18.66 and 10.66.3.211), not the real client. Consequences: (a) the 5/hour bucket is SHARED by ALL visitors hitting the same proxy replica - legitimate users get 429 after 5 total submissions site-wide (reproduced: my pytest run consumed part of the quota and a separate curl client got 429 on its 5th request); (b) a real abuser is never limited individually. The ingress DOES forward the real IP: X-Forwarded-For='34.16.56.64,172.69.59.18,34.160.137.46' (first entry = real client). FIX: custom key_func reading the left-most X-Forwarded-For entry with get_remote_address fallback, e.g. def client_ip(request): xff = request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for'); return xff.split(',')[0].strip() if xff else get_remote_address(request). Consider also raising the limit (5/hour is very tight for a school-facing contact form) and using a shared storage_uri if more than one backend replica runs in production.

minor.issue: slowapi's default handler returns {"error": "Rate limit exceeded: 5 per 1 hour"} - the frontend only reads err.response.data.detail, so users see the generic 'Si è verificato un errore. Riprova.' instead of a 'troppi invii, riprova più tardi' message. Add a custom RateLimitExceeded handler returning {'detail': '...'} (429) or handle status 429 in App.js.

asyncio.create_task(send_notification_email(...)) result is never referenced; the task can be garbage-collected and exceptions are swallowed silently in edge cases. Prefer FastAPI BackgroundTasks or keep a strong reference to the task.
CORS_ORIGINS is still '*' in backend/.env; the credentials logic is now correct, but production deploy must set the real domain(s) explicitly.

ui_bugs.issue: Mobile drawer links and its CTA had NO data-testid (only the hidden desktop nav had nav-*), so automated tests resolved the invisible desktop link and failed. FIXED by testing agent: added data-testid="mnav-<label>" for the 7 links and "mnav-cta" for the CTA. Functionality itself was fine.

issues: og:image and twitter:image point to /og-image.svg but the file does NOT exist in /app/frontend/public - the URL falls back to index.html (200 text/html), so social previews (WhatsApp/Facebook/Twitter) will show no image. Add the og-image.svg (or a PNG, which more scrapers support) or remove the tags.
canonical link is href="/" (relative) - canonical must be an absolute https URL; it is also identical on /privacy since it is static in index.html.
sitemap <loc> values are relative ('/', '/privacy'); the sitemap protocol requires absolute URLs - Google will reject the entries.
robots.txt 'Sitemap: /sitemap.xml' must also be an absolute URL.
Pre-existing from iteration 1: the fixed 'Ho bisogno d'aiuto' FAB overlaps text at the bottom of long sections/footer; consider bottom padding.

action_items: CRITICAL: replace slowapi key_func get_remote_address with an X-Forwarded-For-aware key function, otherwise the 5/hour limit is shared by all visitors (real users will be blocked) and per-abuser limiting does not work.
Return the rate-limit error as 'detail' (or handle HTTP 429 in App.js) so users get a meaningful Italian message instead of the generic error.
Add the missing /public/og-image.svg (or drop og:image/twitter:image) and make canonical/sitemap/robots URLs absolute.
Set CORS_ORIGINS to the production domain(s) before deploy (currently '*').
Optional: use BackgroundTasks instead of a bare asyncio.create_task for the Resend notification.
critical_code_review_comments: Honeypot logic is correct: 'website' is excluded from model_dump before persistence, empty string is treated as human, and the fake success response returns a throwaway uuid - verified in MongoDB that nothing is stored.
The limiter is applied inside the route decorator stack correctly and does NOT consume quota on 422 validation errors (Pydantic rejects before the endpoint runs) - good.
slowapi default in-memory storage means the quota resets on every backend restart/deploy and is per-process; acceptable for a single replica, but note it for production scaling.
lifespan migration is clean (startup/shutdown logged, motor client closed on shutdown); no deprecation warnings in supervisor logs.
App.js is 610 lines and still holds every section component; consider splitting sections into /components for maintainability.

rca_of_the_issue: Rate limiting defect RCA: slowapi's get_remote_address returns request.client.host. In this Kubernetes/Cloudflare setup the FastAPI app sees the ingress/proxy pod address (10.66.x.x) as the peer, so all real clients routed through the same proxy replica collapse into one bucket. Reproduction: 12 rapid POSTs to the public /api/contact returned an interleaved 200/429 pattern (two proxy IPs x 5 quota), and a fresh test client received 429 on its 5th request because an earlier client had already consumed one slot. A debug log confirmed X-Forwarded-For carries the real client IP as the first entry, so a custom key_func fixes both the false positives and the ineffective per-abuser limiting.
